title: dataref: one address for a stored value, and a Secret that prints as stars
intention: Any stored value in Cairn can be pointed at by one address: the scheme names the root (cairn:, cairncommons:, instance:, claude:, file:) and # walks inside the record. It is read through one thin Dataref, and a secret: address hands back a Secret that prints as ********** and gives its value only through .secret.
why: Akien, 2026-11-09, on CC0AC's file:secrets.env#KEY: 'it looks like the perfect way to do file pointers for everything', then 'a class. it's __str__ would return ********** but it's .secret would return the value fetched from the file.' Every reader of a config value re-derives its path and its parse (web_operator._env_value, ccfox env_value, CC0AC private.py), which is Law 1's defect, and a secret held as a plain str prints wherever it is passed.
traces_to: Law 1 (one settled address system instead of a path re-derived per reader); Law 4 (masking a secret is the class's physics, not a habit of care); Law 7 (a miss is loud and names its address); the three-roots rule (credentials in ~/.cairn, so class-space config points and never carries). Outline 17.28.
how: A new tool, cairn/tools/dataref/, above cairn/tools/base/address.py. Its schemes map onto address.ROOTS plus a claude root. urlsplit parses the address; secret: is a one-colon prefix over any whole address. The format comes from the suffix (env, ini/cfg/conf, json), and # walks key, section/key or a/b/c. A file value is cached on (st_ino, st_size, st_mtime_ns); a Secret reads fresh and keeps nothing. db: and host addresses refuse loudly as not yet built. web_operator.secret reads through it.

clauses.claim: each built scheme (cairn:, cairncommons:, instance:, claude:, file:) resolves against a temp roots table to the right file, and cairn:/// and instance:/// equal address.resolve's repo/ and instance/ token faces
# walks env #KEY (export and quotes stripped), ini #section/key with interpolation off, json #a/b/c; no # returns the whole text
a Secret's str, repr, f-string, %-format, format() and a logging call never contain the value, .secret does, and pickle.dumps and json.dumps of it raise
a Dataref re-reads a file after an atomic replace (new inode) and after an in-place edit, and does not re-read an unchanged one; a Secret keeps no cached value
a missing file, a missing key, an unknown scheme, a db: address and an address naming a host each raise DatarefMiss naming the address, with no file value in the message
web_operator.secret reads its key through a Secret (no _env_value left), and web_operator's own proof stays green

decisions.text: D1: the tool lives at cairn/tools/dataref/ and imports only cairn.tools.base.address, cairn.tools.base.diagnostic (its classes reach DiagnosticBase) and the stdlib; it never writes.
D2: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause, over a temp roots table, with no live secret read.

D3: web_operator.secret composes Secret('secret:instance:///devices/<holder>/<n>/.env#KEY', roots), and _env_value is deleted; WebOperator reaches DiagnosticBase. Clause 6's tooth lives in web_operator's own proof (RULE 1: a proof measures only its component), keyed 060d2146618c/6.

out: db: and host addresses (outline 17.28.3, 17.28.1.2, later tickets)
ccfox and ccgoogle (host tools outside git)

measured.saw: the same .env line parse written three times: web_operator._env_value (web_operator.py:252), ccfox env_value (~/.local/bin/ccfox:127) and CC0AC private.py; and address.py's ROOTS has no claude root and no #-item face
measured.how: grep -n '_env_value\|def env_value' over cairn and ~/.local/bin, and reading cairn/tools/base/address.py
